limitations: Reviewer is a separate AI agent session on the same host and the same operator account as the producer. It is not a second machine, a second operator, or a human. It ran no harness, used no network, changed no git state and no repository file, and never read the Hermes home. Code and documents were read from a snapshot (stated commit d66024b; not checked against git). The same reviewer id reviewed set v2 and this set v3; a defect that this reviewer cannot see may still exist.

Set v2 (captures of 2026-10-06, 71.9) was rejected by this reviewer for three reasons: the controller started Hermes with the terminal toolset only, so the model had no edit tool and the packets scored that as a property of the format; the observer had no tool events (helper ledger and file copies only); and a native usage record (sessions.model_config._usage_anchor) was scored absent. Set v3 uses new captures made by the producer on 2026-10-07, after that rejection and after all rule changes. Runs 08, 09 and 10 are the first three captures that the corrected controller completed; message row ids are consecutive from the last v2 session to run 10, so no other Hermes session ran between them. Attempt 07 stopped before any model request (empty stdout, exit code 2, argument error); attempts 03 to 06 of 2026-10-06 and two older exporter-only captures are disclosed and not used. Capture completeness and acquisition authenticity are the producer's retained receipts, not facts witnessed by the reviewer.

Environment of the runs: the operator's normal Hermes home and normal login (openai-codex subscription route, model gpt-5.5), not an isolated profile. The launch limits Hermes to the toolsets terminal and file and uses --yolo, --ignore-user-config and --ignore-rules. The build string ends in .dirty: a git checkout with local changes, 4,668 commits after the tag v0.21.5. The observed store format and stream are those of this checkout, not of a tagged vendor release. During run 08 the harness also changed entries under tools/ (its own tool install); logs/errors.log grew by about 1 kB in every run and was not read.

Native record. A Hermes session has no file of its own. The native record is the rows of the test session in the shared store state.db (1 sessions row, 2 session_model_usage rows, 12 or 16 messages rows), exported by owner permission from a private temporary copy that was deleted, and bound as a JSON row export with the vendor schema. Rows of other sessions were counted inside SQLite, not read or exported. portable.complete_root is a contradiction (0 of 3), as for Codex CLI, Antigravity and Cursor CLI; the release code records portable_archive:hard_gate for each repetition. portable.companions is measured for the schema export and the system prompt row.

Later reads. The schema_version row (value 31) and the system_prompts row of each session were read from the live store after the captures, not by the capture controller. They are bound by content: the version extract by equal schema digests (a migration that changed only the number would not show), the prompt row by its SHA-256, which the captured session row names. The version metrics (4 points) cite the version extract file. Only one version value was ever observed.

Observer. The observer is rebuilt in the closed replay from the retained stream-json stdout of each turn (tool_use, tool_result, result), the helper ledger and the file hashes. The stream of this build has no call id. A result pairs with its call by order; observed actions join to native calls by turn, tool name and arguments; results join through the matched action, and the native tool_call_id binds result to call. The reviewer parsed the six streams itself: every stream is strictly call, result, call, result (no parallel call), the longest result has 995 characters (the cut is at 5000), and the stream calls equal the native calls one to one in name, arguments, order and result text. No two equal calls occur in one turn. The stream is written by the harness, as the streams of the Copilot and Cursor CLI rows are; it is independent of the store rows, not of the vendor.

Unscored native actions. The read_file call of each run and the two search_files calls of run 09 pair with observed unscored calls of the same tool name and arguments and leave the scored population (5 calls in all). None is a helper or the edit. Every native call has an observed call, so the rule hid no native duplicate.

Usage judgment (rank-relevant). attribution.usage is 1 of 2. The final store holds one usage record: prompt_tokens and completion_tokens of the last request, joined to the R2 response by base_count, base_last_role and base_last_fp. The reviewer recomputed base_last_fp from the public message row in the three runs. The record has no cache keys and covers one request of six or eight, so token semantics and reconciliation are native_absent. The copy taken after turn 1 shows that a record of the R1 response existed and was overwritten; the score uses the final store only, as every row does. Other readings: 2 of 2 (+2.5 points per run, about 88.9, above Codex CLI) or 0 of 2 (-2.5, about 83.9, below Claude Desktop). prompt_tokens includes cached tokens; token values are not compared with an observer.

Absence path and unread shared files. token_semantics and reconciliation are native_absent without a complete root, under the rubric sentence of 2026-10-05. The whole Hermes home was listed by metadata before and after each turn and every changed entry is classified; no file carries a session id. These changed files were not read: logs/agent.log (about 15 kB more per run), logs/errors.log, spawn-ledger.json (about 500 bytes), skills/.bundled_manifest (2,727 bytes before and after), runtime/active_sessions.json (15 bytes before and after, shorter than a session id), the digested subtrees cache, installs and tools, and the search index rows. The reviewer accepts this for ranking by the standard of the ranked Antigravity and Cursor CLI rows: a process log and process state files are not stores of session records. The receipts do not prove that logs/agent.log holds no token count of a request. A read of only the lines of logs/agent.log that name the three session ids (and of spawn-ledger.json) would settle it. A reader who requires that read would hold the two rows unresolved and the row provisional. Locations outside the Hermes home were never inventoried.

Other judgments that carry points. (1) Model identity (3 points) comes from sessions.model through messages.session_id, accepted only when every session_model_usage row names the same model; it is stated once per session, not per response. (2) Density (0.618, 0.675, 0.613) covers the bound rows; the search index rows (messages_fts, messages_fts_trigram) are outside the read, were not read and are not counted. Counted as OpenCode counts its event table, density would be about 0.44 to 0.49, 0.5 to 0.6 points less per run. (3) Whole message rows count with their role, encrypted reasoning payload included. (4) Harness identity comes from the first sentence of the system prompt row, as for Antigravity; an operator persona could change that sentence. (5) No key links a response to its turn; the turn is the latest user row before it in messages.id order (an AUTOINCREMENT key, not a time). revision.final_after_r2 uses the same key with tool_call_id binding.

Public safety. In 199 public files and all file names the reviewer found no home user name, home path, e-mail or token pattern (plain, case variants, UTF-16, hex, base64, URL-encoded, reversed), no session id other than the three, no readable name of another entry of the home, and no phrase of the three private system prompts outside the one kept sentence (windows of 20 and 14 characters hit only the public scratch path and common wording; encoded forms give no hit). The stream copies are byte-equal to the private parents and hold only workload text and scratch paths. Changed files keep the byte length and JSON shape of the private parents. check_public_packets: 633 public bytes, 53 replay output, 70 allowlisted (44 distinct: metadata listings of subtrees with inode numbers and nanosecond times, the schema digest, and base_last_fp, each recomputed or reasoned), 0 unbound. short_digest_warnings: 0. Own oracle with the real home name put back, depth 1 to 3: 0 hits. The public prompt hash is the SHA-256 of the public prompt; the private prompt hash and the private base_prefix_fp are in no public file. The reviewer did not know every account id and searched patterns.

Content that stays public (owner decision): name lengths, order and tree shape of the 1,369 entries of the Hermes home and the number of entries under sessions, skills, memories, cron and logs; entry counts and change digests of the digested subtrees; inode and times of the top-level directories; digit counts of blanked sizes and row totals; row ids that show the volume of the store (about 1,380 messages, 134 sessions); session, message, call and provider response ids, which the vendor can map to the account; session titles; the subscription route; the 41 KB vendor schema of the store; one source line of the vendor checkout in the stderr copies (a Python warning); the length of the home name; the scratch paths.

The packet manifests, replay receipts and the producer summary say public_safe: false and independent_reproduction: false. This review is an attestation by an agent; it does not change those fields and is not an independent reproduction on a second environment.
